text: Hoffmann's preface states that his chief difficulties were nomenclature and classification, and gives as an example that the same mechanical puzzle is sold by different dealers under different names.
author: R3 · phase-4 editorial session (2026-09-08)
evidence: Preface, scan page 3: "The chief difficulties I have found in compiling the present collection have been nomenclature and classification."

Preface, scan page 4: "a mechanical puzzle is frequently described in the price-lists of different dealers by different names, the 'Arabian Mystery' of one being, say, the 'Egyptian Paradox' or the 'Ashantee Difficulty' of another."

text: Hoffmann cites Bachet de Méziriac's Problèmes plaisants et délectables as a source for the river-crossing puzzles, dating it 'as far back as 1613'.
author: R3 · phase-4 editorial session (2026-09-08)
evidence: Chapter IV, scan page 177: "that of Bachet de Mezeriac, Eecueil de Problemes plaisants et delect ables qui se font par les nombres, bearing date as far back as 1613."
note: An earlier draft added that the first edition is 'in fact 1612'. That could not be confirmed against an authority record in the time available — Open Library returns a 1959 reprint and the Internet Archive an 1884 Labosne edition, neither of which states the original date — so the counter-claim was CUT rather than softened, per Article 6. The edition now reports Hoffmann's dating as his own and asserts nothing against it.

text: The five chapters selected for this volume carry 91 of the book's figures; the five chapters left out carry 378. The two halves are 39,438 and 40,465 source words respectively.

text: Hoffmann names Paul Perkins and Edward Montauban in his preface as the friends who helped him compile the collection.
author: R3 · phase-4 editorial session (2026-09-08)
evidence: Preface, scan page 4: "a substantial debt of thanks to the many friends (notably Messrs. Paul Perkins and Edward Montauban) who have lent helping hands".
BUILD/source_facts.py over the DE-HYPHENATED whole-book text: montauban 1, perkins 1.
note: Counted against the raw pages the answer is zero, because the preface breaks the name as 'Montau-\nban'. A negative claim written on that answer would have been false and unfalsifiable by re-reading the sentence around it — the Phase 3 British Goblins defect exactly. The fact-checker de-hyphenates before counting for this reason.
